why: Walking a nested list lazily is a DFS you can pause: keep an explicit stack of (list, position) frames, and hasNext unwinds the stack until its top points at an integer without consuming it.
hints: Flattening everything up front works for these sizes, but think about how to produce values on demand.
Keep a stack of (list, index). To find the next integer: pop finished lists, descend into sub-lists, stop when the top points at an integer.
hasNext runs that settle step and reports whether the stack is non-empty; next settles, returns the integer and bumps the index. Amortised O(1) per call, O(depth) memory.
pitfalls: Empty inner lists (even nested ones like [[]]) contribute nothing; hasNext must skip them and may return false.
hasNext must not consume: calling it twice in a row sees the same value.
Parse the input with a JSON parser; output integers as decimal strings, keeping negatives and zero.
